name: Yellow Orange (Color Wheel)
lede: Yellow-Orange (Color Wheel) names the exact midpoint between yellow and orange on the traditional artist's color wheel, a position rather than a pigment or dye.

sections.title: A wheel position, not a pigment
sections.body:
Our library files Yellow-Orange (Color Wheel) from Wikipedia's color lists, under the family word [[yellow]], marking a spot on the color wheel rather than a named material [1]. The parenthetical "(Color Wheel)" exists because other systems, such as Crayola's crayon lists, use the same words for a different hex value [1].

The nearest named color in our look-alike data is [[dark-orange]], 2.9 units away, with [[deep-saffron]] and [[sun-yellow]] close behind at 3.0 [2]. [[tangerine]], 4.7 units off, reads darker [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this exact orange in 0.09 percent of 23,781 paintings, 21 of them as photographed, rarer than 61 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1800s, found in 0.2 percent of the 8,345 paintings we have from then, 15 of them, 1.6 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it plays an accent 96 percent of the time [3]. The earliest dated match is a 1438 panel by Filippo Lippi, though the archive's early centuries are thin enough that this is a floor, not a first [3].
